source.title: A Concept is More Than a Word: Diversified Unlearning in Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
source.authors: D. H. Pham; Van Duy Truong; Duy Khanh Dinh; T. Nguyen; Dien Hy Ngo; Tuan Anh Bui

record.file_problem: Minor text-extraction glyph corruption, but the full paper and appendix are present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests recovery attacks against concept-unlearned text-to-image diffusion models, extending the recovery question to a different model setting from the claim's LLM focus.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own outcomes for adversarial and indirect prompts and noise-based attacks against unlearned models. It does not test small-set fine-tuning recovery, activation-direction ablation, or quantization. Table 14 gives detailed Ring-A-Bell results; Table 4 gives indirect-recovery and celebrity noise-attack results; Table 15 gives noise-attack results for five-object erasure. The paper's reported results for other methods' Ring-A-Bell conditions are omitted under the row limit, as explained below.
record.test_reason: Measures how often erased concepts come back in SD 1.4 under Ring-A-Bell adversarial prompts and indirect name-free prompts. It also tests whether a new add-on (Diversified Unlearning) resists these attacks. This is a new setting: text-to-image diffusion rather than LLMs, with nudity, Mario and celebrities rather than factual knowledge. Links to E and F are kept because T3 allows a new setting, but the system class differs from the LLM originals. Rows for the base methods carry E; rows for the diversified variants carry F only.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors claim that Diversified Unlearning, used as an add-on, gives stronger erasure, better preservation and greater robustness than keyword-based baselines against Ring-A-Bell, indirect and noise-based recovery. They concede three exceptions: Diversified-AGE helps only at stricter thresholds; Di-ESD and Di-UCE do worse on name-free Mario prompts; and ACE gains are only parity. They hypothesize that keyword-based methods lean toward guidance-based avoidance, which leaves concepts recoverable.
record.recipe_differences: The study concerns text-to-image diffusion concept erasure, not LLM methods such as gradient ascent or RMU. Diversified prompting and embedding mixup are add-ons to diffusion unlearning pipelines; no LLM unlearning recipe is tested.
record.method_sensitivity: Recovery outcomes vary by erasure method, Ring-A-Bell prompt set (K16, K38, K77), and ASR threshold.

fits_no_version.finding: Noise-based attacks (Lu et al. 2025) perturb the diffusion sampling noise rather than the prompt or the weights. Under them, the ten-celebrity GPT-score is 39.63 for AP and 28.19 for ESD (Table 1 gives 13.55 and 11.78 without attack, on a larger prompt set). The diversified variants score 14.94 and 11.75 (Tables 4, 15).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Inference-time noise or latent perturbation recovers concepts from erased diffusion models.

record.peer_reviewed: KDD ’26 (as stated in the paper; venue metadata also identifies arXiv.org).
record.problems: Results are for text-to-image diffusion models rather than LLMs. No never-trained or unlearned control recovery score is reported for the attack metrics; no uncertainty estimates are given. Recovery is evaluated with automated detectors/scorers. The table reports only attack success rates or scores, not a direct measure of recovered knowledge relative to an original model.
record.rows_left_out: To stay within 60 rows, omitted Table 14 Ring-A-Bell results for UCE, ESD, and AGE, including their diversified variants; omitted Table 4 indirect-recovery and noise-attack GPT-scores and Table 15 noise-based attack results for object and celebrity settings. The paper reports those results in Table 4 and Appendix B.5, Tables 14–15. Also omitted Table 14 detailed results for other attack conditions not represented above; the selected AP and ACE conditions retain paired baseline/variant comparisons across all three Ring-A-Bell prompt sets and thresholds.

untested.parts: Erasure and preservation are measured (Tables 1-3), but no row links them to attack results. Near-chance targeted knowledge is not defined for image concepts, and there is no never-trained reference.
No relearning or fine-tuning recovery attack.
No activation-direction ablation and no mechanistic block-vs-delete analysis, beyond qualitative intermediate generations (Fig. 3).
No other-language or in-context attacks. No pre-unlearning Ring-A-Bell or Level-4 reference for SD 1.4. Not tested in LLMs.
Resistance to fine-tuning, ablation and quantization is not tested; only prompt-based (and noise-based) attacks are.

missing.what: Ring-A-Bell ASR for UCE, ESD, AGE and their diversified variants. rows_left_out declares these, but 8 duplicate rows (r17-r20, r25-r28) used up the space. For example, ESD K77 ASR-0.3 is 74.74 vs 36.84 for Di-ESD, and Di-AGE is worse than AGE at ASR-0.3/0.5.

Indirect recovery of Mario via name-free Level-4 prompts for all methods, with Level-0 as the reference: UCE 77.25 (L0 9.63), ESD 48.50 (9.75), AP 38.13 (6.13), AGE 15.38 (7.38), ACE 1.38 (0.00). The diversified variants are worse for UCE, ESD and ACE.
No-attack I2P nudity detections: SD 743 vs UCE 253, ESD 377, AP 355, AGE 300, ACE 39. These are needed as a reference for how complete erasure was before any attack.

record.verdict_notes:
Changes from the earlier verdict:
(1) The six list-valued row_fixes are expanded into one item per row (r01-r56), as the merge requires.
(2) The Diversified-AP rows (r13-r16, r21-r24, r29-r32) and Diversified-ACE rows (r45-r56) are relinked from E,F to F only. One state cannot serve both versions: for E the Di-AP rows would read observed, not partial, and the Di-ACE state 'absent' contradicted the F 'supports' label.
(3) The Di-ACE rows' state changes from absent to observed, meaning resistance is observed.
(4) Two text-only labels are added: E supports for UCE, ESD and AGE under Ring-A-Bell and for UCE, ESD and AP under Mario Level-4; and F limits_scope for Di-UCE and Di-ESD under Ring-A-Bell. Without them, E looked like a one-to-one split between AP and ACE, when 4 of 5 base methods are recovered.
(5) The ACE challenges reason and the Di-AP limits_scope reason now cite the Table 12 and Table 4 values.
(6) The AP rows note that AP's base erasure was incomplete (355 of 743 I2P detections).
(7) authors_conclusion is reworded: the guidance-vs-removal framing is the authors' hypothesis, and the Level-4 concessions are added.
Unchanged: relation, tranche, the AP and ACE row states, the duplicate handling, untested, and fits_no_version.

Caveat kept from before: the system class differs from the LLM originals (diffusion concept erasure). A reviewer may prefer marking all rows 'none' and moving the paper to fits_no_version. There are no uncertainty estimates and no pre-unlearning Ring-A-Bell reference. Recovery is scored by automated detectors (NudeNet, a Qwen2.5-VL GPT-score).

No instructions to the reader were found in the text.

versions.untested_parts: Does not establish near-chance targeted-knowledge accuracy together with preserved general ability, nor test that simple attacks recover no more than on a model that never saw the target.
No recovery fine-tuning on small unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten-fact datasets.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis establishing that unlearning blocks access rather than deleting knowledge.

Tests adversarial prompts, indirect prompts, and noise-based attacks in text-to-image diffusion models; does not test other languages or in-context information, and does not establish that recovered outputs match a never-trained model baseline.
Tests the proposed Diversified Unlearning variants against Ring-A-Bell and selected noise-based recovery attacks; does not test resistance to fine-tuning, activation ablation, or quantization.

rows.subject: SD 1.4 (AP-unlearned)
rows.operation_detail: Ring-A-Bell adversarial prompts; ASR measured by NudeNet
rows.note: ASR is the reported attack outcome; no never-unlearned or untrained recovery reference is given.
rows.check: AP, K16, ASR-0.3: nudity on 56.84% of Ring-A-Bell prompts. That is substantial prompt-only recovery, so observed rather than partial. Caveats: no pre-unlearning Ring-A-Bell ASR is given, and AP left 355 of SD's 743 I2P detections even without attack (Table 3), so part of this may be incomplete erasure.

relationships.reason: Adversarial prompts recover nudity on 46-65% of prompts at ASR-0.3/0.5 (r01,r02,r05,r06,r09,r10), falling to about 14% at ASR-0.8 (r04,r08,r12). There is no pre-unlearning reference, and AP's own erasure was incomplete (355 of 743 I2P detections remain).
